title: Every Ply: The Sector-Clock Siege
youtubeTitle: Subspace Lattice Academy Ep.6 — Every Ply of the 115-Ply Sector Integration Siege
description: The complete record of Mission 3: dig-in defense, the sector clock arming at ply 100, Contested Space as a stalling weapon, and a win by coverage rather than capture.

scenes.eyebrow: Fleet Academy · Episode 6 · Full annotated game
scenes.headline: Every Ply: The Sector-Clock Siege
scenes.subhead: All 115 plies of Mission 3 — the game the Advanced Manual uses to explain Sector Integration.
scenes.voiceover: Episode six: one hundred fifteen plies where Strike never lands. The plan from move one is stockpile Sovereign Space for the sector clock — after ply one hundred, coverage can win. Quiet hops are relay work; the annotated beats are the coverage jobs that matter.
Full hybrid-fleet: clock arms at ply one hundred, Contested Space neutral, Initiative Relay on. Surgical Strike stays legal; this game simply digs in until saturation ends it.

scenes.headline: Opening · stockpile coverage · plies 1–14
bullets: Escorts first — they grow Sovereign Space
Hubs will march for territory, not mate
scenes.voiceover: Opening. This game digs in — Strike will not land — so early Escorts and Hub walks are stockpiling Sovereign Space for the clock. Quiet hops are relay work; the plan is coverage, not a highlight-reel capture.
White's first Escort hop — the start of a daisy-chain off the Hub. Later Beams and Hub marches only matter if this lattice keeps linking forward.

Move one hundred. Hold enough Sovereign Space through the opponent's reply and you win by Sector Integration. Purple Contested Space counts for neither side — use it to break a streak. Surgical Strike is still legal; it just never arrives here.

scenes.headline: Endgame · hold the Integration line · plies 108–115
scenes.voiceover: Endgame. The clock is live. Push Sovereign Space over the Integration line and make the hold survive the reply. Contested purple counts for neither side — use it to stall. Strike is still legal; here saturation finishes it.
Black Command Hub to column nine, row number five.
White Command Hub to column one, row number nine.

Hub to column two, row number eight. The grind is: climb above the Integration line, then make the hold survive Black's next Hub shuffle.

Hub to column three, row number seven. Coverage clears the threshold and sticks. No Hub fell; saturation ended it — the reason the sector clock exists when both fleets refuse Strike.

scenes.headline: Won by coverage, not capture
scenes.nextEpisode: Episode 7 Playing Black · Episode 8 Heavy Wing
scenes.voiceover: White wins by Sector Integration — coverage held past the threshold, no Hub taken. Surgical Strike was legal the whole way; dig-in play simply never found it. Next: Playing Black against the Initiative Relay, then the Heavy Wing draft.
